definition: Cross-modal retrieval is a subfield of information retrieval that enables users to search for and retrieve information across different data modalities, such as text, images, audio, and video.
details: Unlike traditional information retrieval systems that match queries and documents within the same modality (e.g., text-to-text search), cross-modal retrieval bridges different types of media to facilitate more flexible information access.

explainer.lead: Cross-modal retrieval lets you use one kind of media to find another, such as typing a description and getting back images or videos. It makes collections of different media searchable without requiring every query and result to have the same format.

tiers.eli5: Imagine describing “a dog catching a ball” and having a library bring you a matching photo, sound recording, or video. Cross-modal retrieval works like a translator between your description and those different kinds of media, helping you find things even when they do not contain your exact words.
tiers.practitioner: A system typically converts queries and candidate media into representations that can be compared, then ranks candidates by their compatibility with the query. Applications need data that captures meaningful cross-media relationships; otherwise, results may share superficial features while missing the query’s intent. Evaluation should test retrieval across modality pairs rather than only same-modality search.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a query q in modality A and candidates x in modality B, cross-modal retrieval ranks candidates by a compatibility score s(q, x) and returns the highest-ranked items. The central problem is comparing semantically related content across different representations. Performance can be limited by ambiguous queries, weak alignment between modalities, and media whose relevant meaning is difficult to represent.

explainer.example: A user enters “a red bicycle beside a lake.” The system compares this text query with an image collection and returns pictures showing that scene, even when the pictures themselves are not text documents.

usedIn.name: Multimedia search
usedIn.detail: Finding images, audio, or video from queries expressed in another modality.

usedIn.name: Digital libraries and archives
usedIn.detail: Providing flexible access to collections containing several kinds of media.

usedIn.name: Media asset management
usedIn.detail: Locating relevant visual or audio material without relying only on text search.

explainer.intuition: Different media can describe the same underlying thing: a sentence, a photograph, and a video may all depict a dog catching a ball. Cross-modal retrieval compares that shared meaning so a query in one medium can find relevant content in another.
howItWorks: Accept a query in one modality, such as text.
Represent the query and candidate media so their compatibility can be compared.
Compare the query with candidates from the desired modality.
Rank and return the most compatible candidates.
explainer.whyItMatters: People often know how to describe what they want without having a query in the same format as the desired content. Cross-modal retrieval makes mixed-media collections more flexible and accessible to search.
misconceptions: It is not ordinary text search with media filenames or captions; the defining feature is retrieval across different modalities.
It does not require returning every modality at once; a text-to-image search is already cross-modal.
A returned item is not guaranteed to match perfectly, because cross-media compatibility can be ambiguous.
